overview: COVID-19 is a disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus, which spreads through the air in infectious respiratory particles from an infected person. Most people recover without treatment, but some may develop severe disease. The virus can also spread by touching contaminated surfaces and then the eyes, nose or mouth.
symptoms: muscle aches and heavy arms or legs
runny or blocked nose, or sneezing
appetite loss, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or diarrhoea
loss or change of sense of taste or smell
persistent pain or pressure in the chest
skin being cold or clammy, or turning pale or a bluish colour
transmission: airborne transmission through infectious respiratory particles
close contact with an infected person
touching contaminated surfaces and then the eyes, nose or mouth
prevention: single dose for persons who have not yet received a COVID-19 vaccine
risk_factors: health and care workers due to their work environment
people with chronic lung, heart, liver and/or kidney diseases
complications: multiorgan failure, including injury of the heart, liver or kidneys
post COVID-19 condition (PCC, or long COVID)
key_facts: about 6% of people develop post COVID-19 condition (PCC, or long COVID)
symptoms usually begin 3-6 days after exposure and last up to 10 days
